social support network size is associated with relationship satisfaction, and that relationship satisfaction is associated with psychological well-being.

(a) social network size is associated with lower levels of stress and depressive symptoms, and with higher levels of life satisfaction, and that (b) these associations are mediated by relationship satisfaction; (c) the relationship between proportion kin and lower levels of stress, and higher levels of life, satisfaction is mediated by relationship satisfaction, but not by depressive symptoms.

relationship satisfaction is a key factor in the association between social support network characteristics and older adults' psychological wellbeing, and that this is a key finding in the literature.

social network characteristics (e.g., network size, network composition) are related to psychological well being, but this relationship is mediated through relationship satisfaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quality of social relationships is a more salient factor for psychological well being than the quantity of social relationships.
older adults who are satisfied with their relationships have better mental health.
older adults' satisfaction with their social relationships is a critical factor in their psychological well being.

social relationships are important for well being in late-life, and that the qualitative aspects of these relationships may be more important than the quantitative aspects.
